fact.claim: If a global secondary index does not have enough capacity to handle updates, DynamoDB throttles writes to the base table to maintain data consistency; this is called GSI back-pressure.
fact.question: What is GSI back-pressure?

values.display: throttles writes to the base table

evidence.quote: If a GSI doesn't have sufficient capacity to handle these updates, DynamoDB throttles writes to the base table to maintain data consistency.
evidence.title: Understanding Global Secondary Index (GSI) write throttling and back pressure in DynamoDB
